benchmark: identity-quality: how reliably does ECDEV read product identifiers and decide that two observations are the same product?
method: policy-permitted product pages sampled from retailers' own sitemaps (ECDEV robots evaluator and AI-agent policy, 2 s per host, ECDEV user agent, plain HTTP, no browser); an independent parser (json.loads over every ld+json script, microdata and meta regexes, a visible-label pass, own check-digit code) states what each page says; ECDEV's own extractor and its fixture resolution say what ECDEV recovered; Open Library edition records give a second, explicitly identified source for books

hosts.japanese_finding: no stated JAN in static HTML on any of 12 pages (13-digit JANs appear only inside image file names on sofmap.com and books.rakuten.co.jp, which assert nothing); JAN evidence therefore comes from Open Prices and Yahoo Shopping, not retailer pages

source_coverage.visible_only_pages: ravensburger.de and libraccio.it listing/author pages naming several editions; a visible label there is not the page subject

extraction_recall.before_fix_first_66_pages: 9 of 17 valid stated codes (JSON-LD gtin, gtin13 and microdata gtin13: 9 of 9; JSON-LD isbn: 0 of 5; visible labels and a nested identifier: 0)
extraction_recall.the_miss: braun.de /about/identifier (a PropertyValue under an about node), 1 page
fixes: JSON-LD isbn extracted (hyphenated ISBN-13 and ISBN-10 normalised by the ISBN standard, stated value kept)
isbn on workExample for Product+Book (booktopia.com.au: 12 pages)
a node carrying both offers and a product code is a product under any type (exlibris.ch Book and MusicAlbum)

normalization_matrix: domain/commerce/src/resolution.rs::identifier_matrix_normalizes_by_standard_and_never_repairs (GTIN-8/12/13/14, padded forms, bad check digits, bad lengths, separators, letters, numbers, all-zero, ISBN-13 with hyphens or spaces, ISBN-10 including X)

cross_source_matching.retailer_to_retailer: 0 cross-host product overlaps in 280 pages: no cross-retailer positive pair exists in this sample, so retailer-to-retailer precision and recall are NOT measured

positive_pairs_using_the_first_listed_id.note: the 3 non-merges are Open Library records that list several editions' ISBNs; the first one names a different edition, so not merging is right

store_to_open_library.unresolved: 11 of 24 bookstore ISBNs are not in Open Library (no pair)

cross_source_matching.sample_reuse: the ISBN-10 conversion was added because this benchmark showed 9 of 13 positives unmerged; the 13/13 is a demonstration on the sample that exposed the gap

conflicts: real structured data: 0 pages with two different valid codes; the conflict case is pinned by fixture (conflicting_valid_codes_stay_a_visible_conflict_and_never_merge) and was a silent SKU fallback before this wave
variants: hifi-regler.de publishes one distinct valid EAN per variant (3 variants, 3 codes) and ECDEV keeps three identities; logitech.com states one mpn per ProductModel, which ECDEV reads only as a blob on the parent product, so those variant MPNs are not separate identities
official_lookup_invariant: already implemented and tested (adapter/marketplace/src/reads.rs catalog_search: an item answers a requested code only when its own identifiers list that code, compared as GTIN-14); benchmarked, not rewritten; fixture only, no credentials
native_changes: CONFLICTING_GTIN_CLAIMS instead of a silent SKU fallback
identifier_claims, identifier_state and identity_next_step on every resolution (stated value, state, normalised form kept apart)
all-zero code is not a GTIN
blank identifier is not a claim
isbn in JSON-LD annotate (and on workExample for Product+Book)
offers + product code makes a product under any @type
deliberate_no_change: visible-label identifier extraction: visible codes equalled structured codes on 54 of 54 pages and the visible-only pages are multi-edition listings, so it would add wrong subject attributions
fuzzy or title matching: the unresolved remainder cannot be judged without cross-retailer overlap; title near-duplicates stay uncertain links
limits: 35 hosts fetched, 11 with a structured valid code, mostly Nordic/German electronics and books; no Japanese retailer page states a JAN
no cross-retailer overlap so no retailer-to-retailer precision/recall; product-family vs variant identity not exercised beyond variant EANs
one capture time; fixture resolution (the same code path as a live run, fed captured bytes)
Open Library is an open catalogue, not an authority; a record listing several ISBNs is itself conflated
